title: Wrong pixel scale for VGGnet
body: Hi I just noticed that for the whole algorithm the pixel values for network input output are scaled to 1 to 1 However The VGG16 network is supposed to take input tensors with pixel range 0 to 255 The following code in the vgg16 py scales the pixel range to 510 to 0 rgb scaled tf subtract input image tf ones like input image 2 255 The VGG weights are set as constant and not trained I doubt that the VGG net is not able to extract proper features for the edge information because of the wrong scaling So problem rises that if the VGG net is really needed for edge guided purposes or edge information is not helping for this algorithm

comments.body: You re right You found a bug in the current implementation We didn t notice this problem during training Because the pre trained and fixed HED network somehow generated reasonable edge maps with wrong scaled input images which can be seen using Tensorboard Although the detected edges may not be as sharp as being feed with correct scaled input images Also in the ablation studies we conduct an experiment to show that this edge information however with wrong scale may help the network to produce better results We believe that using the correct scaled images CyclicGen may benefits more from the edge information and leads to a better results in PSNR SSIM However we will leave this bug here for the reproducibility of our AAAI paper Thank you very much for your report
I guess you wanted to put tf divide but mistakenly typed tf subtract Anyways interesting idea and nice work Enjoyed reading the paper

title: High resolution with larger displacement
body: Hi alex04072000 Thank you for your great work When I test your model on high resolution image with larger displacement the interpolated frame became blurry As this sample shows 1080 1920 sample https user images githubusercontent com 38717829 50325967 b4b07180 0522 11e9 9e24 df80aed7073d png Would you give some ideas about this issue Using traing datasets with larger displacement or enlarging receptive field

comments.body: Thank you for being interested in our work This blurry result is caused by exteremely large motions The motions shown here are even larger than the receptive field of the network There will be 2 straight forward solutions for this problem 1 Train a larger network with more layers to increase the receptive field 2 Downscale the input frame pair As our main target is UCF 101 dataset the receptive field of our baseline model is quite small

Thanks for your suggestions The two stage framework proposed in your paper is very different from bidirectional optical flow based and make it much easier for interpotation It might be possible to come up with more new approaches based on this framework
